direction.name: Asymmetric Mediterranean Garden House
direction.concept: A single-storey Mediterranean garden house formed as a connected asymmetric L around a sheltered, inward-looking garden. The longer social wing combines open-plan kitchen, dining and living spaces with generous garden glazing and a covered veranda; the shorter private wing provides three bedrooms and two bathrooms along calm, comfortable circulation. Warm ivory plaster, pale limestone detailing and terracotta pitched roofs establish a clear main-roof hierarchy without detached structures or changes in terrain.
hierarchy: A dominant pitched-roof social wing anchors the composition and contains the open-plan kitchen, dining and living rooms facing the sheltered garden.
A lower, perpendicular private wing forms the second arm of the L, containing three bedrooms, two bathrooms and a quiet internal circulation spine.
A recessed shaded entrance sits at the inside bend of the L, mediating between arrival and the protected garden court.
A covered veranda extends from the social wing toward the garden, with the terrace and modest pool positioned as integrated outdoor rooms rather than separate objects.
direction.roofLanguage: Terracotta clay-tile pitched roofs give the house its Mediterranean character. A broad, dominant main roof covers the social wing, while a lower perpendicular pitched roof distinguishes the bedroom wing. Deep eaves shade glazing and veranda edges; roof junctions remain simple and legible, reinforcing the asymmetric L-shaped massing.
direction.entrance: A shaded, recessed entrance is placed at the protected inner corner of the L. Pale limestone threshold, surround and restrained wall detailing give arrival a durable civic emphasis, while the approach remains deliberately modest and sheltered beneath the roof overhang.
direction.outdoorLiving: The covered veranda faces directly into the sheltered garden and connects seamlessly to the open-plan kitchen, dining and living area through room-proportioned glazing. A limestone-toned terrace expands beside the veranda for dining and lounging, while a modest swimming pool is set within the garden court with clear sightlines from the social rooms.
direction.landscape: The flat site is treated as a restrained Mediterranean garden: clipped low hedging, gravel-edged planting beds, small groups of drought-tolerant shrubs, aromatic herbs and a limited number of slender shade trees. Planting frames the sheltered court, softens pool edges and preserves open arrival space around the connected house volumes.
